newsitem.title: USA: Bellcore declines comment on possible sale of labs.
newsitem.headline: Bellcore declines comment on possible sale of labs.

text.p: Bellcore, the research arm of the seven regional Bell companies, declined to comment on a report that the research labs would be sold for about $700 million to SAIC, a San Diego-based defense contractor.

In a statement, Bellcore said that, "As of today, the board has made no decision to sell the company. Bellcore cannot comment about any prospective buyers, or about any board deliberations," the statement said.
The report, which appeared in the Wall Street Journal Monday, cited unnamed executives who said the impending sale awaited final approval by the boards of Bellcore's owners.
Morristown, N.J.-based Bellcore is jointly owned by Bell Atlantic Corp, Pacific Telesis Group, NYNEX Corp, Ameritech Corp, SBC Communications Inc, BellSouth Corp and U S West Inc.

SAIC, which stands for Science Applications International Corp, is a privately held company that has close ties to the Defense Department. The Journal said SAIC, which has annual revenues of about $2 billion, was seeking to expand its telecommunications practice by acquiring the Bellcore labs.
SAIC was not immediately available to comment.
The Journal report said International Business Machines Corp and Electronic Data Systems Corp had been among the "early and serious" bidders for Bellcore.
Bellcore's owners had announced in April 1995 that they were considering the sale of their interests in Bellcore.
